meta.phase: 1 - component picking, datasheet parsing, BOM risk
meta.baseline: bom/h11_baseline.json, extracted from the Altium LiveBOM shipped in LCU_H11/LCU_H11.zip
meta.scope: Selection and risk assessment. No schematic capture, no footprints beyond what selection forces.

line_status.changed: exists in LCU_H11 but the part or its role changes
line_status.select: part not chosen yet, candidates listed

criticality.safety: its failure can drop the pod or defeat a safety function
criticality.functional: its failure degrades or stops the mission
criticality.auxiliary: its failure is a nuisance or a loss of visibility

findings.topic: The airgap analog front end exists only in the LCU_H10 BOM
findings.detail: LCU_H11 replaced the 4-20 mA analog front end with a sigma-delta path: the Airgap Sensors sheet in LCU_H11 carries eight DFSDM clock/data pairs (DFSDM_CKOUT_0..7, DFSDM1_HF_DATIN1) and a 5 V filter block built around a DLW43SH110XK2L common-mode choke, not a current-loop front end. The corresponding modulator board is the A-ADC board in the H11 inventory. That path was never brought up, and LCU_H11 firmware reads the airgaps on ADC1, so hardware and firmware disagree in H11.
findings.consequence: H12 reinstates the LCU_H10 circuit: 160 ohm sense resistor, 5th-order Butterworth in the '4-20mA conditioning sub-block', MCP6022, into ADC1. Those parts are NOT in the LCU_H11 BOM, so they must be specified from the LCU_H10 schematic rather than inherited.

findings.topic: The SN74LVC541A in the H11 BOM is there for the wrong reason
findings.detail: Buffer_CK on LCU_H11 is the DFSDM clock buffer: SN74LVC541A with 33 ohm series resistors, driving DFSDM_CKOUT to the eight modulator channels.
findings.consequence: The part and the 33 ohm pattern are already qualified, but the block disappears with the sigma-delta path. It is still the right candidate for the LPU PWM buffers, so the part stays in the BOM with a different purpose.

risk_model.note: Additive score per part; impact adjusts the final priority. Every weight is a judgement, but the arithmetic is explicit and reproducible, which is the point.

STM32H723ZGT6.lifecycle_source: ST product page; H723 remains in the ST long-term availability programme
alternates: STM32H723ZGT6 is effectively sole-source: no pin-compatible second source exists for the H7 family
STM32H723ZGT6.note: Two per board. Supply, not lifecycle, is the risk: H7 parts have had multi-month lead times. Ordering both MCUs early is the single most effective de-risking action on this board.

KSZ8041TLI.lifecycle_source: Microchip application note AN4212 'Migrating to KSZ8081/8091 Family PHY Transceivers' is written for customers using KSZ8041 devices
KSZ8041TLI.note: AN4212 names KSZ8041NL/RNL/MLL, not the TL variant, so this is a family-level signal rather than an EOL notice for the exact part. Carried over from LCU_H11 unchanged; if a respin is ever needed, budget for a pinout change, not a drop-in.

7499011222A.description: RJ45 jack with integrated magnetics and LEDs
7499011222A.lifecycle_source: Wurth product line, carried from LCU_H11 and VCU_H11
alternates: Halo/HanRun/Pulse equivalents exist but are footprint-incompatible
7499011222A.note: Mechanical part: a substitute will almost certainly not fit the same footprint. Treat as a stock item to buy early.

ASE-50.000MHZ-LR-T.description: 50.000 MHz CMOS oscillator, RMII reference clock
ASE-50.000MHZ-LR-T.lifecycle_source: Abracon ASE series, carried from LCU_H11
alternates: Any 3.2x2.5 50 MHz CMOS XO (SiTime SiT8008, ECS, Kyocera)
ASE-50.000MHZ-LR-T.note: Commodity. The RMII reference must come from here rather than from the MCU, which is why the PHY support circuit differs from a resistor-strap-only design.

TJA1051T/3.description: High-speed CAN transceiver, 3.3 V interface, SO-8
TJA1051T/3.lifecycle_source: NXP TJA1051 family, in volume production
TJA1051T/3.note: Two per board, one per MCU, on the same bus. The /3 variant is the one with the 3.3 V logic interface; the plain TJA1051T has 5 V logic and must not be substituted.

SN74AHCT367.lifecycle_source: TI datasheet: 'NRND: Not recommended for new designs. Device is in production to support existing customers, but TI does not recommend using this part in a new design.'
alternates: SN74LVC541A (3.3 V, 8 channel, already in the LCU_H11 BOM)
SN74AHCT367.note: Being replaced in H12. Vendor NRND is objective; the degradation reported in the field is consistent with an unterminated 5 V output driving a cable, which is a design fault independent of lifecycle.

SN74LVC541APWR.lifecycle_source: TI catalogue part, in volume production; already used on LCU_H11 Buffer_CK
SN74LVC541APWR.note: Considered and rejected for the LPU PWM path: it is a 3.3 V part, so its output would never reach the 5 V the LPU needs. It stays in the library only as the record of that comparison; the LCU_H11 Buffer_CK role it was bought for disappears with the sigma-delta airgap path (F-02).

SN74AHCT541.lifecycle_source: TI product page: '8-ch, 4.5-V to 5.5-V buffers with TTL-compatible CMOS inputs'. No NRND notice, unlike the AHCT367.
SN74AHCT541.note: Selected for the LPU output bank. Three signals leave the LCU per LPU -- PWM_1, PWM_2 and RESET -- all at 5 V, so the bank carries 30 signals. The LPU needs 5 V and the MCU drives 3.3 V, which is exactly what an AHCT part is for: TTL-compatible inputs put VIH at 2.0 V, so a 3.3 V MCU output drives it directly with no level shifter, and the output is full 5 V CMOS. RESET is active-low, so releasing it requires an actively driven HIGH, which is why it cannot be open-drain. Eight channels per package: five packages, two LPUs each, six channels used and two spare.

MCP6022-E/SN.description: Dual op-amp, rail-to-rail I/O, 10 MHz, SOIC-8
MCP6022-E/SN.lifecycle_source: Microchip catalogue part, in volume production
MCP6022-E/SN.note: One per airgap channel. The 2.5 mV maximum offset is 125 LSB at 16 bits over 3.3 V, so the amplifier -- not the ADC -- is the accuracy limit together with the sense resistor. Retained for H12 because the topology is retained; an upgrade to OPA2320 is a later decision, not a blocker.

LT1963AEST-3.3.description: 1.5 A low-noise LDO, fixed 3.3 V, SOT-223
LT1963AEST-3.3.lifecycle_source: ADI product page states 'RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS'
LT1963AEST-3.3.note: Carried over. SOT-223 dissipates poorly; confirm the thermal margin once the SD card load is added.

LM5013-Q1.description: 100 V input, 3.5 A non-synchronous buck regulator
LM5013-Q1.note: Carried over. A 100 V input rating implies VIN can be a high rail, which is why the LCU_H10 input voltage is still an open value (TMP/ARCH item). Non-synchronous means an external catch diode, already in the BOM.

TE-5499922-6.description: AMP-LATCH universal header, 26 positions, 2.54 mm, vertical with long latches
TE-5499922-6.lifecycle_source: Not stated on distributor listings; family is stocked and shipping, but no vendor lifecycle statement found
alternates: No drop-in alternative: the LPU harness and the LPU board both assume this footprint
TE-5499922-6.note: Ten per board and frozen by the LPU_H11 interface, so there is no design freedom here -- only a supply question. Verify the lifecycle directly with TE and confirm the 44.5 mm body, which the Phase 0 mechanical figure depends on.

MOLEX-206832-0401.description: Micro-Fit+ vertical header, 4 circuits, 3.00 mm, dual row
MOLEX-206832-0401.lifecycle_source: Molex current catalogue; Micro-Fit+ is the H12 team standard
MOLEX-206832-0401.note: Replaces every Nano-Fit on the board: 8 airgap, 2 bootloader, 2 brake chain, 4 corner NTC. Using one part number for all four functions simplifies both the BOM and the harness crimp tooling.

TPS62130.description: placeholder for any new rail needed by the SD card or the LED driver
TPS62130.note: PLACEHOLDER. There is no evidence a new rail is needed; LT1963A at 1.5 A has margin unless the SD card and the LED driver together add more than a few hundred mA. Delete this line once the power budget is closed.

ICM-42688-P.note: Optional and unpopulated. Chosen over LSM6DSO only because its SPI timing is simpler; if the control team prefers a part they already have drivers for, that wins and this line changes.

160R-0603-0.1pct.lifecycle_source: Commodity thin-film resistor; several vendors in volume production
160R-0603-0.1pct.note: Airgap 4-20 mA sense resistor. 0.1 % is already the accuracy limit at about 10 bits, matching the sensor's own +/-140 um linearity; upgrading to 0.01 %/5 ppm buys nothing until that is solved.

82306050029.description: WE-VE ULC bidirectional ESD suppressor array
82306050029.lifecycle_source: Wurth WE-VE series, currently catalogued; already used on VCU_H11
82306050029.note: Already qualified on the VCU_H11 SD and Ethernet sheets. Standardising on it avoids introducing a second protection part family.

MOLEX-216571-2002.description: microSD card connector, push-push, 9 way, with detect switch
MOLEX-216571-2002.lifecycle_source: Molex memory-card connector family, currently catalogued
alternates: TE 1939115-1 (rejected: no package data, flagged unavailable in the VCU vault)
MOLEX-216571-2002.note: Chosen over the TE part because its footprint and 3D model are already proven in the VCU_H11 design: 216571-2002-Footprint-1 with 216571-2002.stp embedded. Carry the footprint across verbatim rather than re-creating it.

SM712-02HTG.description: Bidirectional asymmetric TVS array for RS-485 / CAN
SM712-02HTG.lifecycle_source: Littelfuse catalogue; already in the LCU_H11 BOM in volume production
SM712-02HTG.note: Intended for exactly this: two data lines of a differential bus. One per CAN node.

VLMTG1300-GS08.lifecycle_source: In the LCU_H11 BOM at Volume Production, distributor stock above 79 000
VLMTG1300-GS08.note: Per-LPU status indicator, twenty pieces: ten on READY and ten on FAULT. Green because its forward drop is about 2.0 V, which leaves 1.3 V across the series resistor on a 3.3 V rail. A blue LED would be a poor choice here: its forward voltage is around 3.0 V, so on a 3.3 V rail the current would be tiny and extremely sensitive to part-to-part spread. If the two indicators need to look different, use an amber 0603 for the health LED rather than a blue one.

VLMS1300-GS08.lifecycle_source: In the LCU_H11 BOM at Volume Production, distributor stock above 32 000
VLMS1300-GS08.note: Not used by the per-LPU indication, which is green on both signals. Kept because it is already in the LCU_H11 BOM driving the firmware-controlled board LEDs (led_fault and friends), which are inherited unchanged.

lines.note: LCU_H11 has a CAN transceiver but the firmware never instantiates FDCAN. H12 wires both MCUs as nodes.

lines.function: LPU output buffer bank: 2 PWM + RESET per LPU, 5 V
lines.note: Five TSSOP-20 packages, two LPUs each: four PWM channels plus two RESET channels, 30 signals in total with ten channels spare. The 1:2 grouping is kept from LCU_H10 because it matches the enable partitioning and the harness order. Four packages would be the arithmetic minimum (32 channels); the fifth costs about EUR 0.40 and 30 mm2 and avoids splitting an LPU pair across packages. Package choice was reviewed in D-07 and confirmed: 16-bit parts reduce count but not area, and the pull-up/pull-down question is settled by RESET being active-low.
Reinstated from LCU_H10 (F-01): LCU_H11 has no analog airgap front end. One MCP6022 per channel. Amplifier supply moves from +5 V to +3.3 V, which is a net change, not a part change.
Reinstated from LCU_H10 (F-01); absent from the LCU_H11 BOM. 0.1 % is already the accuracy limit at about 10 bits, matching the sensor's own +/-140 um linearity.

candidates: MAX7420 if the analog rail stays at 5 V
lines.note:
DEFERRED: a different filter design may be adopted, so this is not being specified now.

Corrected scope: LCU_H10 does not build a discrete filter. The Airgap Sensors sheet uses one switched-capacitor filter IC per channel (MAX7420, 5 V, 5th-order Butterworth), with its corner frequency set by the internal oscillator from a 220 pF capacitor. So the block is eight ICs and a handful of passives, not the eighty discrete parts this line originally assumed.

Knock-on that has to be carried with the deferral: because the analog rail moves to 3.3 V, the 5 V MAX7420 is no longer usable and the equivalent part becomes the MAX7424. That is a forced change of part number, not a preference.

lines.function: Corner NTC excitation and filter passives
candidates: 10 kOhm 0.1 % pull-up to 3V3 + 220 ohm series + 10 nF (mirrors LCU_H11 Temp_conditioning)
lines.note: Values depend on the NTC part, which is the same device as LPU_H11 (Q-15). The 220 ohm / 10 nF values are inherited and only need re-checking against the chosen pull-up.

Taken from the VCU_H11 design after checking both candidates. Molex 216571-2002 has a real footprint and an embedded 3D STEP model (216571-2002-Footprint-1 / 216571-2002.stp) in the VCU design; the TE 1939115-1 has no package data and is flagged Availability=Unavailable in the VCU vault. The verified footprint decides it.
Würth WE-VE ULC array, already in the LCU_H11 BOM and used on the VCU_H11 SD sheet.

lines.function: Per-LPU levitation indicator, driven from READY (lit means levitating)
lines.note: Green 0603 LED plus a 1 kOhm series resistor from each READY line to ground. Lit when that magnet is ready. Together with L-LED-HEALTH this gives two bits per LPU with no logic at all: both lit means levitating, READY dark with FAULT lit means healthy but idle, both dark means faulted or unplugged. Optional and DNP-able. Parts already in the LCU_H11 BOM.

lines.function: Per-LPU health indicator, driven from FAULT (lit means no fault)
lines.note: LED with a 1 kOhm series resistor from each FAULT line to ground. FAULT is active-low, so the LED is lit when the line is HIGH, which is the healthy state: a dark LED means that LPU is faulted or unplugged. Same topology as the READY LED, one resistor each, no inversion, no gate, no transistor.

lines.function: Protection on the analog inputs: 8 airgap loops and 4 corner NTC
lines.note: Protection tier 2: two suppressors per airgap loop (a current loop is less exposed, but the cable runs beside the LPU power leads) and one per NTC line plus a series resistor. Tier 3 would be board-internal signals, which is not proposed.

lines.function: ESD and clamp protection on the LPU lines
lines.note: Protection tier 1: the 50 lines that leave the board on the LPU connectors -- 20 PWM, 10 RESET, 10 READY, 10 FAULT. One WE-VE ULC per line at the connector plus the series resistor already required on the status lines. Absent in LCU_H10 and LCU_H11, so this is an addition, not a swap.

candidates: discrete NPN/MOSFET pulling the enable high
lines.note: One gate: brake_fault AND the MCU enable, into the five package enable pins. RESET is active-low and buffered, so the override cannot act on the reset net; it releases the bank and the pull-downs assert every reset. Firmware must drive the RESET buffer inputs LOW before asserting the enable, otherwise the first enabled instant drives indeterminate levels.

The LCU_H11 BOM carries 49 passive and discrete lines, all in volume production with distributor stock above 5000 except a handful. They are not re-listed individually here; see bom/h11_baseline.json. Re-verify prices at order time, not now.
Already in the LCU_H11 BOM and designed for RS-485/CAN transients. One per transceiver node.

decisions.question: Does the LPU accept 3.3 V logic on PWM_1/PWM_2, or does it need 5 V?
decisions.recommendation: The LPU needs 5 V. SN74AHCT541: TTL-compatible inputs accept the 3.3 V MCU drive (VIH = 2.0 V) and the output is 5 V CMOS. Three TSSOP-20 packages for 20 signals. Active lifecycle, unlike the AHCT367.
decisions.contingency: Both candidates are pin-compatible TSSOP-20, so the footprint can be committed before the answer arrives. Populate whichever is needed.
decisions.answer: LPU PWM input is 5 V; MCU output is 3.3 V. Resolved with SN74AHCT541.

decisions.question: TE 1939115-1 or Molex 216571-2002? Both appear in the VCU_H11 SD documentation.
decisions.recommendation: Molex 216571-2002. Both parts appear in VCU_H11, but only the Molex one has a verified footprint and an embedded 3D model; the TE part has no package data in the VCU design and is marked unavailable in its vault.
decisions.answer: Take the VCU part with the correct footprint: Molex 216571-2002.

decisions.question: What is the protection for, and what does it have to be paired with?
decisions.recommendation: Three voltage classes, not one part number. The claim that a single WE-VE ULC covers everything was wrong: a 5 V standoff part on a 5 V logic line sits right at the rail and leaks, and the same part on the 24 V brake chain is useless. Use a 6 V class on the 5 V LPU signals, a 5 V class on the 3.3 V status and analog lines, and a 30 V class on the brake chain. CAN keeps SM712-02HTG, which is already the right asymmetric 24 V part.
decisions.note: The clamp is the second half of the protection, not the first. What actually limits current into a pin is the series resistor: with a 9 V clamp into a 3.3 V pin, a 100 Ohm resistor still pushes 57 mA through the internal diode, and 1 kOhm brings it to 5.7 mA. So the order of priority is series resistor per line first, clamp second, and the clamp chosen so its standoff sits above the signal's maximum level. See the Phase 1 document, section 3.6.

decisions.question: Keep the MCP6022 or move to a lower-offset part?
decisions.recommendation: Keep for H12. The sensor's own linearity limits performance to ~10 bits, so a better amplifier changes nothing measurable until that is fixed. Revisit only if an accuracy requirement appears.

decisions.topic: Reset buffering and the brake override
decisions.question: How can brake_fault assert the LPU resets if RESET is a push-pull 5 V buffer output?
decisions.recommendation: Through the buffer enable, not through the output. RESET and the two PWM lines share the 5 V bank; the enable is active-low and pulled to disabled, and brake_fault forces it disabled in hardware. The RESET lines then fall to the asserted level through their pull resistors, and the PWM outputs go high-impedance.
decisions.note: This supersedes the open-drain wired-AND described in Phase 0 section 6.3, which cannot work against a push-pull buffer. Consequence to design for: a released bank also releases the PWM lines, so the LPU PWM inputs need pull-downs of their own, otherwise they float at the far end.

decisions.topic: Buffer bank: part choice and package count
decisions.question: Is there a buffer arrangement that takes less space than 5 x SN74AHCT541?
decisions.note:
Channel count is fixed at 30 (2 PWM + RESET per LPU) unless RESET stops being buffered. Package footprints below are body sizes; total area is the package area multiplied by the count.

| Option | Part | ch/pkg | Package | Body mm | mm2/pkg | Pkgs | Total mm2 | mm2/ch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | SN74AHCT367 | 6 | TSSOP-16 | 5.0 x 4.4 | 22.0 | 5 | 110 | 3.7 |
| B | SN74AHCT541 | 8 | TSSOP-20 | 6.5 x 4.4 | 28.6 | 4 | 114 | 3.6 |
| C | SN74AHCT541 | 8 | TSSOP-20 | 6.5 x 4.4 | 28.6 | 5 | 143 | 3.6 |
| D | SN74AHCT244 | 8 | TSSOP-20 | 6.5 x 4.4 | 28.6 | 5 | 143 | 3.6 |
| E | SN74AHCT16244 | 16 | TSSOP-48 | 12.5 x 6.1 | 76.3 | 2 | 152 | 4.8 |
| F | SN74AHCT16244 | 16 | TVSOP-48 | 9.7 x 4.4 | 42.7 | 2 | 85 | 2.7 |
| G | unbuffered RESET, 3 x SN74AHCT541 | 8 | TSSOP-20 | 6.5 x 4.4 | 28.6 | 3 | 86 | 3.6 |

The arithmetic that matters: the 8-channel TSSOP-20 is the area sweet spot at 3.6 mm2 per channel. Going to a 16-bit part does NOT reduce area -- the TSSOP-48 variant is 4.8 mm2 per channel, worse than the octal -- it only reduces part count. The 16-bit part wins on area only in the 0.4 mm-pitch TVSOP package, which is hostile to hand assembly.
decisions.recommendation: Keep option C: SN74AHCT541, five TSSOP-20 packages, two LPUs each. The octademal is the area optimum at 3.6 mm2 per channel; the 16-bit alternative saves part count but not area unless it is the 0.4 mm-pitch TVSOP, which only pays off in a reflowed build. Five packages keep each LPU pair on one package and leave ten spare channels.
decisions.note_2: Option G is the largest saving of all -- 30 percent less area and two fewer packages -- but it is only available if the LPU RESET input is active-HIGH. An active-low reset has to be released by driving it high, which needs a push-pull driver, and a pull resistor cannot hold it in the asserted state when the driver is released. LCU_H10 firmware calls turn_on() on the reset lines to enable the LPUs, which suggests active-low, so option G is probably unavailable. Confirm the polarity before spending time on it.
decisions.decision_needed: None. Revisit only if the board moves to a reflow process, which would make the TVSOP-48 option worth re-costing.
decisions.answer: LPU RESET is active-low: driving it HIGH releases the reset and lets the LPU work. That makes the release state an actively driven HIGH, which a pull resistor cannot provide, so the buffer is mandatory. Option G is ruled out.

decisions.question: Driver IC on the MCU, or indication built from the signals themselves?
decisions.answer: Two hardware LEDs per LPU, both driven directly from the status line with nothing but a series resistor: green on READY, lit when levitating, and a second LED on FAULT, lit when there is no fault. No driver IC, no inverter, no diode-OR, no MCU pins, no firmware.
decisions.recommendation: Drive both status lines active-high and let a dark LED mean the bad state. READY lights when ready; FAULT lights when healthy. Forty parts in total, all 0603, all optional, and the same topology repeated twenty times.
decisions.note:
The first version tried to indicate a fault with a lit red LED, which fails because FAULT is active-low: the LED has to sink current into the line, and with the connector unseated the only return is the 10 kOhm pull-down, which lifts the line to about 0.9 V against a VIL of about 1.0 V. That would make the presence detector marginal exactly where it matters.

Indicating the ABSENCE of a fault instead removes the problem completely: the LED sits from FAULT to ground like the READY one, so it conducts only when the line is HIGH. Un-driven, the pull-down holds the line at 0 V, the LED stays off and draws nothing, and the logic level is untouched. Same topology for both signals, no inversion anywhere.

The cost is that the fault indication is now the absence of light rather than a red lamp coming on. For a bench diagnostic that is acceptable, and the board already has firmware-driven LEDs (the LCU_H11 five) for an at-a-glance alarm if one is wanted.

datasheet_index.note: Drop PDFs into H12/LCU/datasheets/ named by MPN and rerun bom/build.py. The parser reads them with pdftotext and looks for the parameters listed per part.
